ref_extractions.title: Temporal scaling of human scalp-recorded potentials
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper directly examines temporal scaling in human EEG/MEG data across four datasets, including interval perception and production tasks. It develops a GLM-based approach with variable-duration regressors specifically designed to unmix fixed-time and scaled-time components in scalp-recorded potentials.
ref_extractions.paradigm: Temporal scaling/interval timing (production and perception tasks)
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Variable-duration regressors spanning cue-to-response intervals; GLM-based deconvolution approach
ref_extractions.label_mapping: Interval conditions (short/medium/long) encoded by trial duration variation
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Strong methodological alignment with the temporal scaling dataset paradigm; the variable-duration GLM approach directly addresses how to analyze temporally scaled responses in interval production/perception tasks.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Directly uses human EEG data to study temporal scaling phenomenon. Analyzes interval timing tasks including production and perception. Four independent EEG datasets analyzed. Method paper for analyzing scaled-time components in human scalp potentials.

feasibility_reason: The dataset has a well-defined temporal scaling paradigm with 18 distinct condition/phase combinations encoded in trigger codes, and one reference paper (paper_10_1073_pnas_2214638119.pdf) directly supports EEG-based temporal interval classification tasks for production and perception conditions.
tasks_section:
## Tasks

### Classical Task 1: Temporal Condition Multiclass Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 1.0 s, overlap = null, target_events = [11, 12, 13, 17, 21, 22, 23, 27, 31, 32, 33, 37, 41, 42, 43, 47, 51, 52, 53, 57, 61, 62, 63, 67]
- **Label Route**: `Annotation`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:

 | Event | y | Meaning |
 |-------|---|---------|
 | `11` | 0 | Production Cond 1 Phase 1 |
 | `12` | 1 | Production Cond 1 Phase 2 |
 | `13` | 2 | Production Cond 1 Phase 3 |
 | `17` | 3 | Production Cond 1 Feedback |
 | `21` | 4 | Cond 2 Phase 1 |
 | `22` | 5 | Cond 2 Phase 2 |
 | `23` | 6 | Cond 2 Phase 3 |
 | `27` | 7 | Cond 2 Feedback |
 | `31` | 8 | Cond 3 Phase 1 |
 | `32` | 9 | Cond 3 Phase 2 |
 | `33` | 10 | Cond 3 Phase 3 |
 | `37` | 11 | Cond 3 Feedback |
 | `41` | 12 | Cond 4 Phase 1 |
 | `42` | 13 | Cond 4 Phase 2 |
 | `43` | 14 | Cond 4 Phase 3 |
 | `47` | 15 | Cond 4 Feedback |
 | `51` | 16 | Cond 5 Phase 1 |
 | `52` | 17 | Cond 5 Phase 2 |
 | `53` | 18 | Cond 5 Phase 3 |
 | `57` | 19 | Cond 5 Feedback |
 | `61` | 20 | Cond 6 Phase 1 |
 | `62` | 21 | Cond 6 Phase 2 |
 | `63` | 22 | Cond 6 Phase 3 |
 | `67` | 23 | Cond 6 Feedback |

- **Evidence**: DOI: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2214638119 | DOI: https://doi.org/10.18112/openneuro.ds004200.v1.0.1
- **Kernel Notes**: Event `2` (block boundary, N=3542) excluded as admin marker. Feedback events (7x) have variable counts (~550-907) indicating differential trial counts across conditions. This is the primary decoding task for temporal scaling representations across all experimental conditions and phases.

### Classical Task 2: Temporal Production Long Event Analysis
- **Task Type**: segmentation
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_long_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0.0 s, tmax = 5.0 s, overlap = null, segment_length = null, target_events = [17, 27, 47, 57, 67]
- **Label Route**: `Annotation`
- **Meta Level**: super
- **Target Definition**:

 | Event | y | Meaning |
 |-------|---|---------|
 | `17` | 0 | Production feedback offset (Cond 1) |
 | `27` | 1 | Cond 2 feedback offset |
 | `47` | 2 | Cond 4 feedback offset |
 | `57` | 3 | Cond 5 feedback offset |
 | `67` | 4 | Cond 6 feedback offset |

- **Evidence**: DOI: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2214638119
- **Kernel Notes**: Aligned to feedback offset markers (7x events) which mark production completion. Variable-duration paradigm with 5s window capturing the full production period and feedback response. Derived from raw event alignment; high-level meta reflects trial-level production outcome. Tens digit encodes task type (1x=production per paradigm description).

### Normal Task 1: Interval Length Binary Discrimination
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 1.0 s, overlap = null, target_events = [11, 12, 13, 17, 21, 22, 23, 27, 31, 32, 33, 37, 41, 42, 43, 47, 51, 52, 53, 57, 61, 62, 63, 67]
- **Label Route**: `Annotation`
- **Meta Level**: super
- **Target Definition**:

 | Event | y | Meaning |
 |-------|---|---------|
 | `11` | 0 | Short interval |
 | `12` | 0 | Short interval |
 | `13` | 0 | Short interval |
 | `21` | 0 | Short interval |
 | `22` | 0 | Short interval |
 | `23` | 0 | Short interval |
 | `31` | 1 | Medium interval |
 | `32` | 1 | Medium interval |
 | `33` | 1 | Medium interval |
 | `41` | 1 | Medium interval |
 | `42` | 1 | Medium interval |
 | `43` | 1 | Medium interval |
 | `51` | 2 | Long interval |
 | `52` | 2 | Long interval |
 | `53` | 2 | Long interval |
 | `61` | 2 | Long interval |
 | `62` | 2 | Long interval |
 | `63` | 2 | Long interval |

- **Evidence**: DOI: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2214638119
- **Kernel Notes**: Binned interval length classification (short/medium/long) reducing 6-condition multiclass to 3-class problem for improved statistical power on N=20 dataset. Condition mapping to interval lengths requires verification from paradigm description.

### Potential Task 1: Production vs Perception Task Separation
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 1.0 s, overlap = null, target_events = [11, 12, 13, 21, 22, 23, 31, 32, 33, 41, 42, 43, 51, 52, 53, 61, 62, 63]
- **Label Route**: `stim`
- **Meta Level**: super
- **Target Definition**:

 | Event | y | Meaning |
 |-------|---|---------|
 | `11` | 0 | Production task |
 | `12` | 0 | Production task |
 | `13` | 0 | Production task |
 | `21` | 1 | Perception/judgment task |
 | `22` | 1 | Perception/judgment task |
 | `23` | 1 | Perception/judgment task |
 | `31` | 1 | Perception/judgment task |
 | `32` | 1 | Perception/judgment task |
 | `33` | 1 | Perception/judgment task |
 | `41` | 1 | Perception/judgment task |
 | `42` | 1 | Perception/judgment task |
 | `43` | 1 | Perception/judgment task |
 | `51` | 1 | Perception/judgment task |
 | `52` | 1 | Perception/judgment task |
 | `53` | 1 | Perception/judgment task |
 | `61` | 1 | Perception/judgment task |
 | `62` | 1 | Perception/judgment task |
 | `63` | 1 | Perception/judgment task |

- **Evidence**: Paradigm description states tens digit encodes task type (1x=production, 2x-6x=other conditions)
- **Kernel Notes**: Binary discrimination between active interval production and passive interval perception/judgment. Derived from super-level meta using tens digit mapping. Excludes feedback events (7x) and admin marker (event 2).

### Potential Task 2: Temporal Scaling Error/Performance Analysis
- **Task Type**: regression
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_long_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = 0.0 s, tmax = 5.0 s, overlap = null, segment_length = null, target_events = [17, 27, 47, 57, 67]
- **Label Route**: `Annotation`
- **Meta Level**: super
- **Target Definition**:

 | Event | y | Meaning |
 |-------|---|---------|
 | `17` | 0 | Production trial 1 (normalized temporal error) |
 | `27` | 1 | Production trial 2 (normalized temporal error) |
 | `47` | 2 | Production trial 4 (normalized temporal error) |
 | `57` | 3 | Production trial 5 (normalized temporal error) |
 | `67` | 4 | Production trial 6 (normalized temporal error) |

- **Evidence**: Plausible from paradigm; temporal scaling literature (DOI: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2214638119) uses production error as dependent variable
- **Kernel Notes**: Requires external annotation of produced vs. target interval error. Trial-level labels must be derived from behavioral data (key press timestamps). Would examine neural correlates of temporal scaling accuracy. Production task (1x) not present in feedback events—using available 2x-6x feedback events as proxy for production-related conditions.
